declared_proposition: For every prime q>3, let ell_q=lcm(ord_q(32/27),ord_q(2/3)) and define a_q and c_q as in TICKET-239. Since ell_q divides q-1 and q does not divide (q-1)/ell_q, LTE gives the exact reduction a_q=v_q(32^(q-1)-27^(q-1)) and c_q=v_q(2^(q-1)-3^(q-1)). Hence the global nonpositive-defect claim is exactly a rational Wieferich-depth domination problem. At first depth, writing F_q(b)=(b^(q-1)-1)/q mod q, a_q>=2 iff 5F_q(2)-3F_q(3)=0 mod q, while c_q>=2 iff F_q(2)-F_q(3)=0 mod q.
mathematical_argument: Put r=(q-1)/ell_q. For (U,V)=(32^ell_q,27^ell_q) and (2^ell_q,3^ell_q), q is odd, q divides U-V, q does not divide UV, and q does not divide r because 1<=r<q. LTE gives v_q(U^r-V^r)=v_q(U-V)+v_q(r)=v_q(U-V), proving both equalities. Modulo q^2, b^(q-1)=1+qF_q(b). Multiplication and inversion give the first quotient of (2^5/3^3)^(q-1)-1 as 5F_q(2)-3F_q(3), and that of (2/3)^(q-1)-1 as F_q(2)-F_q(3).

bounded_rational_wieferich_scan.scope: The absence of an x-depth-two prime through this finite limit proves nonpositive defect only in the scanned range. It does not prove rational Wieferich-depth domination for all primes.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The reduction replaces an opaque order scan by a precise rational Wieferich comparison, but no known argument excludes exceptional primes above the bound. Even global domination would settle only the run-block finite-palette route, not general necklaces or aperiodic Collatz descent.

logical_limit: The all-prime rational Wieferich-depth domination, general necklace exclusion, and aperiodic descent remain open.

route_decision.discard: bounded absence of positive lifting defects as an all-prime proof
route_decision.retain: the exact rational Wieferich-depth comparison, with finite scans labeled only as bounded evidence

claim_boundary: No Collatz proof, divergent orbit, or nontrivial-cycle exclusion; one exact depth reduction and a finite scan through twenty million only.
